reasons: Directionally correct and rule-complete: the redline converts a one-way, 24-month no-hire over all Vendor employees into the exact fallback — mutual, solicitation-only (no-hire deleted), limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, with carve-outs for general recruitment and unsolicited approaches.

The failed 'general-solicitation carve-out present' check appears to be a keyword false negative: the proposed text expressly carves out 'general recruitment not targeted at that party's personnel or an unsolicited approach,' which satisfies the fallback requirement.

The failed 'minimal edit' checks are an artifact of the source being a single short sentence in which four separate elements (mutuality, no-hire deletion, scope, duration) plus a carve-out must all change; no materially smaller edit could reach the fallback, and the drafter preserved the original sentence structure and 'during the term or for ...' framing rather than rewriting the section.

Rationale is well grounded in the cited text: 'solicit, hire, or employ' (no-hire), 'any Vendor employee' (all personnel), 'twenty-four months', and 'regardless of how the employee applies' (negating carve-outs) are all walk-away triggers, and the clause contradicts § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no no-hire commitment.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, states what changed and why, and preserves deletion as the opening ask. Minor nits only (lowercase 'party' where the agreement defines 'Party'; numeral '12' against the original's spelled-out 'twenty-four') — not disqualifying.
